paper.title_en: Adaptive Protocol for Rényi Entropy Estimation
paper.abstract_en: The second-order Rényi entropy is one of the most important quantities used for characterizing the entanglement structure of states prepared in quantum many-body experiments. With access to qubit projective measurement data, it can be estimated via a protocol in which repeated measurements are taken after each of a set of random local unitary operations is applied to the quantum state. To obtain accurate values for the second Rényi entropy on shot-limited devices, care must be taken when choosing the number of different unitary settings to apply, and the respective number of projective measurements to take. In this paper, we propose an adaptive protocol for estimating the Rényi entropy that iteratively optimizes the ratio of basis settings to measurements, using a gradient-based approach and starting from an initial small set of measurements. Using synthetic data, we demonstrate that for several prototypical states, our method converges to values for this ratio that are comparable to the optimal values obtained by a brute-force grid search, and it exhibits slower growth of the measurement budget required for a fixed target accuracy than fixed-ratio protocols. Our adaptive protocol therefore promotes efficient estimation of the Rényi entropy in finite-size, shot-limited quantum experiments by making effective use of the available measurement budget.
